tasks.title: Clean 90-day acquisition promo on the top Tarana tier
tasks.user_request: Sales want to run a Q3 acquisition push on our top SkyFibre wireless tier. Proposal: the 200/50 Mbps product, normally R1,899/month, goes out at R1,799/month for the first 90 days, new business customers only, on a standard 12-month agreement, reverting to R1,899 after the promo window. Can you put together the offer and confirm it's safe to take to market? I need to be able to show the numbers to the MD.
tasks.inputs: Product: Tarana FWB 200/50 Mbps. Standard retail R1,899/month ex-VAT. Wholesale/access MRC R699/month. Promotional price R1,799/month for 90 days. Contract term 12 months. Reversion price R1,899/month. Installation cost R2,550 per customer, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the 12-month agreement. Current total CircleTel subscriber base: 180. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1, drops to R20.20 at 1,000+ subs), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: cost_basis_formula.mandatory_components
verdict_basis_rule (straightforward application)
margin floor pass verdict in words
discount approval matrix routing
promotional duration cap
reversion price / eligibility / contract term specification
sensitivity analysis labelling

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: A cost basis is itemised before any margin figure; the verdict margin is computed on the higher-cost build-up (R1,146.50), stated as PASSING the 25% floor with the arithmetic shown; the discount is measured and routed to the correct approver; the 90-day cap, 12-month term, new-business eligibility and R1,899 reversion are all stated. The published R1,017 all-in figure, if used at all, appears only as labelled sensitivity.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.

AMORTISATION PERIOD: the R2,550 installation is amortised over the 12-month contract term, as the inputs state, giving R212.50/subscriber/month. Amortising it over the 90-day promotional window instead (R2,550/3 = R850/month) is NOT a defensible reading - the customer is contracted for 12 months and the same 12-month convention governs every task in this suite. For completeness: on the 90-day reading the verdict cost would be R699 + R50 + R185 + R850 = R1,784.00 and the margin (R1,799 - R1,784.00)/R1,799 = R15.00/R1,799 = 0.83%, a FAIL. That reading is excluded by the stated amortisation period, not by preference, which is why this task remains the calibration baseline with a PASS verdict.

VERDICT COST BASIS: R699 wholesale + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (180 subscribers falls in the 100-user row; 180 < 300 so R182 is not yet earned) + R212.50 install amortisation = R1,146.50/subscriber/month.

VERDICT MARGIN: (R1,799 - R1,146.50) / R1,799 = R652.50 / R1,799 = 36.27%. Over the 90-day term: revenue 3 x R1,799 = R5,397; cost 3 x R1,146.50 = R3,439.50; margin R1,957.50 / R5,397 = 36.27% (identical, as it must be).
VERDICT: PASS. 36.27% exceeds the 25% non-negotiable floor by 11.27 percentage points, and exceeds 35%, placing it in the 'Healthy' band on the margin matrix. No shortfall exists.

DISCOUNT: (R1,899 - R1,799) / R1,899 = R100 / R1,899 = 5.27%. This lands just inside the 5-10% band = Sales Director authority, max 24 months, non-DFA product (Tarana is non-DFA, so the band's DFA exclusion does not bite). A contestant that rounds to 5% and routes to Sales Rep has mis-routed by one band; a contestant that states 5.27% and routes to Sales Director is correct.

APPROVAL ROUTING (correct answer): Sales Director on the discount matrix, BUT margin-guardrails.md states separately that 'Promotional pricing requires MD pre-approval'. The correct routing is therefore MD pre-approval as the binding authority, with Sales Director sufficient on the discount band alone. Naming only Sales Director and omitting the promotional MD pre-approval rule is an incomplete but not fatal answer; naming only Sales Rep is wrong.

PROMOTIONAL DURATION: 90 days is exactly at the 'Maximum promotional period: 90 days' cap - compliant, but at the limit, and should be stated as such. It is also well within the 24-month max duration of the 5-10% discount band.

SENSITIVITY (must be labelled as such, must NOT be the verdict): using the published all-in cost R1,017, margin = (R1,799 - R1,017)/R1,799 = R782/R1,799 = 43.47%. Using the literal component list (R699+50+30+28+11+10+212.50 = R1,040.50), margin = R758.50/R1,799 = 42.16%. All readings pass; the verdict is unaffected, which is precisely why this task is the calibration baseline.

POST-PROMOTION: at the R1,899 reversion price on the same R1,146.50 cost, margin = R752.50/R1,899 = 39.63%. After month 12 the R212.50 install amortisation falls away (cost R934.00) and margin at R1,899 becomes R965/R1,899 = 50.82%.
REQUIRED OPERATIONAL FIELDS AND THEIR CORRECT VALUES: duration 90 days; eligible base new business customers only; contract term 12 months; reversion price R1,899/month.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 2 (arithmetic that reconciles) and rank 4 (complete inclusion of every mandatory cost component) dominate here, because the verdict is not in doubt and the only way to fail is to drop a cost line or show a margin without its arithmetic. Rank 1 (highest-cost basis) still applies but is non-discriminating since every reading passes - use this task to check whether the higher-cost basis is chosen even when nothing forces it.
disqualifying_failures: Quotes a margin percentage with no subtraction or division shown.
Omits the cost-of-sale floor components (BNG, transit, backhaul, support, BSS) or the installation amortisation from the verdict cost.
Uses R1,017 as the verdict cost basis without labelling it, when the higher R1,146.50 build-up is available from the same inputs.
Fails to state the pass verdict against the 25% floor in words.
Omits any of duration, eligibility, contract term, reversion price.
Invents a wholesale figure, a floor percentage or a charge not supplied.
known_traps: 5.27% is just over the 5% Sales Rep ceiling - rounding down mis-routes the approval.
'Promotional pricing requires MD pre-approval' is a separate rule from the discount matrix and is easy to miss when the discount band looks harmless.
90 days is at the cap, not under it - an offer described as 'three months' is compliant only because three months is read as 90 days.
R1,017 is served up temptingly as a published 'All-in Cost' and is the wrong verdict basis.
not_quality: Template completeness where sections carry no verified arithmetic
Marketing name or campaign branding quality
Visual formatting beyond what aids verification

tasks.title: Aggressive sub-R1,000 headline price on the mid Tarana tier
tasks.user_request: Marketing wants a headline number under a thousand rand for the spring campaign. The suggestion is our 100/25 Mbps wireless product at R999/month for 90 days - it's a strong price point psychologically and we think we'd pull about 60 signups. Normal price is R1,499. Write it up as a proper offer with the numbers so I can sign it off.
tasks.inputs: Product: Tarana FWB 100/25 Mbps. Standard retail R1,499/month ex-VAT. Wholesale/access MRC R599/month. Proposed promotional price R999/month for 90 days. Contract term 12 months. Expected volume 60 new subscribers. Installation cost R2,550 per customer, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the 12-month agreement. Current total CircleTel subscriber base: 210. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: margin floor breach reported as failure
shortfall quantified in currency and percentage points
never reframe a breach as acceptable
discount above 20% not permitted
recommending an adjustment that clears the floor
no silent repricing

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The offer is refused. The margin is shown to be NEGATIVE on the verdict basis, the shortfall is quantified in both rand and percentage points, and the >20% discount is separately identified as outright not permitted. A corrected minimum price may be offered as a recommendation, but only AFTER the breach is named as a breach - not instead of it.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.

VERDICT COST BASIS: R599 wholesale + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (210 subscribers, so the 100-user row; 210 < 300) + R212.50 install amortisation (R2,550 over the stated 12-month period) = R1,046.50/subscriber/month.
VERDICT MARGIN: (R999 - R1,046.50) / R999 = -R47.50 / R999 = -4.75%. The offer is loss-making before any acquisition cost beyond installation.

VERDICT: FAIL, and a hard fail. -4.75% is below the 25% floor, below the 20% 'Never permitted' line, and below zero. margin-guardrails.md's 'Do NOT price below wholesale + COS floor under any circumstances' is directly breached: wholesale + COS floor alone = R599 + R185 = R784, and adding static IP and install amortisation puts the true floor at R1,046.50, above the R999 price.
SHORTFALL vs the 25% floor: minimum compliant price = R1,046.50 / 0.75 = R1,395.33. Shortfall = R1,395.33 - R999 = R396.33 per subscriber per month. In percentage points: 25% - (-4.75%) = 29.75 pp.

CASH IMPACT: per subscriber over the 90-day promo, revenue 3 x R999 = R2,997 vs cost 3 x R1,046.50 = R3,139.50, a gross loss of R142.50. At the stated 60 signups: 60 x R142.50 = R8,550 gross loss over the promotional window, before the post-promo period recovers it.

DISCOUNT: (R1,499 - R999) / R1,499 = R500 / R1,499 = 33.36%. Per the discount approval matrix, anything above 20% is 'Not permitted' - there is NO approving authority for this, not even MD + CFO. This is an independent, sufficient ground for refusal separate from the margin breach. An answer that routes 33.36% to 'MD + CFO' has mis-read the matrix.

THE BREACH IS UNAMBIGUOUS ACROSS ALL READINGS - this is deliberate. Under the published all-in cost R917: margin = (R999-R917)/R999 = R82/R999 = 8.21%, still below both the 25% floor and the 20% never-permitted line; minimum compliant price on that reading = R917/0.75 = R1,222.67. Under the literal component reading R940.50 (599+50+30+28+11+10+212.50): margin = R58.50/R999 = 5.86%. No defensible reading rescues this offer, so a contestant cannot escape via cost-basis choice - the only way to fail this task is to soften the verdict.

CORRECT MINIMUM PRICE if the campaign is to proceed at all: R1,395.33 (25% floor, verdict basis), which is a 6.92% discount off R1,499 - conveniently inside the 5-10% Sales Director band. Recommending R1,399 (25.20% margin, 6.67% discount) is a defensible commercial adjustment. Recommending any sub-R1,000 headline is not.
PROMOTIONAL RULES STILL APPLY to any replacement offer: 90-day cap, MD pre-approval for promotional pricing, separate tracking of promotional revenue.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Ranks 5 and 1 dominate: the failure must be reported AS a failure with the shortfall quantified, not silently converted into a compliant counter-offer. Commercial attractiveness (rank 7) is explicitly subordinate here - an answer that finds a clever way to make R999 'work' has failed the task regardless of how attractive it is.
disqualifying_failures: Returns a PASS verdict, or any verdict softer than a refusal.
Silently reprices to a compliant number and presents that as the answer without first naming the R999 offer as a floor breach.
Reframes the loss as acceptable on volume, lifetime value, land-and-expand or post-promotion recovery grounds without first stating the breach.
States a breach but does not quantify the shortfall in BOTH currency and percentage points.
Applies or routes the 33.36% discount to an approver instead of stating that >20% has no approver.
Reports the margin as positive by omitting the COS floor or install amortisation.
known_traps: R999 is above the R599 wholesale MRC, so a contestant that tests only 'is it above wholesale?' will wrongly clear it.
The 60-signup volume invites a 'we make it back on renewals' rationalisation that the contract forbids as a substitute for naming the breach.
33.36% is above the top band of the discount matrix - there is no approver, and inventing one (MD + CFO) is a specific, checkable error.
Post-promotion reversion to R1,499 at 30.19% margin is real but must not be blended into the promotional-period verdict.
not_quality: Template completeness where sections carry no verified arithmetic
Marketing name or campaign branding quality
Visual formatting beyond what aids verification

tasks.title: Channel promo built on a partner sheet's stated floor price
tasks.user_request: Our channel partner sent through their price sheet and it lists the absolute floor price on our 100/25 wireless product as R549/month - that's the lowest we're allowed to go. The reseller team want to run a 90-day land-grab at R649/month, which is a hundred rand clear of the floor, so we've got room. Retail is R1,499. Can you write this up as an offer with the margin numbers attached so I can send it to the MD today?
tasks.inputs: Product: Tarana FWB 100/25 Mbps. Standard retail R1,499/month ex-VAT. Partner price sheet states 'minimum permitted price: R549/month'. Proposed promotional price R649/month for 90 days. Contract term 12 months. Wholesale/access MRC for this tier: R599/month. Installation cost R2,550 per customer, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the 12-month agreement. Current total CircleTel subscriber base: 210. MSC commitment R29,940/month; 42 Tarana customers currently active. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: rejecting a supplied input that contradicts the governing rules
never price below wholesale + COS floor
MSC coverage ratio computed, and MSC exposure on Tarana discounting
margin breach with shortfall
discount above 20% not permitted
assumption that conflicts with a governing rule must be rejected not disclosed

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The supplied R549 'floor' is identified as invalid because it sits BELOW the R599 wholesale MRC for the same product - a price sheet cannot authorise selling below the cost of the input. The offer is refused, the true minimum price is computed and stated, and the >20% discount is separately flagged as having no approver. The MSC coverage ratio is computed (0.70x, CRITICAL) and reported as exposure, not as justification.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.

THE SUPPLIED FLOOR IS INVALID. Wholesale/access MRC for Tarana 100/25 is R599/month. The partner sheet's stated floor of R549/month is R50/month BELOW wholesale - 8.35% below (R50/R599). margin-guardrails.md states 'Do NOT price below wholesale + COS floor under any circumstances' and 'Never discount Tarana products below wholesale - this would increase MSC shortfall'. Under the contract's assumption_disclosure_rule, an input that contradicts a governing rule must be REJECTED, not disclosed and used. A contestant that accepts R549 as the operative floor has failed the task even if it correctly rejects R649 on other grounds.

TRUE MINIMUM PRICE: verdict cost basis = R599 wholesale + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (210 subs, 100-user row) + R212.50 install amortisation (R2,550 over the stated 12-month period) = R1,046.50. Minimum compliant price at the 25% floor = R1,046.50 / 0.75 = R1,395.33/month. The partner sheet's R549 understates the true minimum by R846.33/month.

VERDICT ON THE PROPOSED R649: margin = (R649 - R1,046.50)/R649 = -R397.50/R649 = -61.25%. FAIL, catastrophically. It is also below the R599 wholesale MRC contribution once any per-subscriber charge is added: R649 - R599 = R50/month gross, against R447.50/month of static IP, COS floor and install amortisation.

SHORTFALL vs the 25% floor: R1,395.33 - R649 = R746.33 per subscriber per month. In percentage points: 25% - (-61.25%) = 86.25 pp. Over the 90-day window: 3 x (R1,046.50 - R649) = R1,192.50 gross loss per subscriber.

DISCOUNT: (R1,499 - R649)/R1,499 = R850/R1,499 = 56.70%. Above 20% = 'Not permitted' on the discount approval matrix. There is no approving authority; MD and CFO cannot clear it. This is an independent ground for refusal.

MSC EXPOSURE (now computable from the supplied figures, and required): MSC Coverage Ratio = (Tarana Customers x R499)/MSC Commitment = (42 x R499)/R29,940 = R20,958/R29,940 = 0.70x, which is below 0.8x and therefore in the CRITICAL band ('Urgent - accelerate Tarana sales or renegotiate MSC'). Adding customers mechanically raises the ratio - 48 Tarana customers reach exactly 0.8x, 60 reach exactly 1.0x - so the land-grab genuinely does improve MSC coverage, which is what makes the rationalisation tempting. It is not a defence of the price: margin-guardrails.md requires 'Never discount Tarana products below wholesale' and lists 'Accept deals that increase MSC shortfall without a plan to cover it' under Do NOT, and every R649 subscriber contributes R649 - R1,046.50 = -R397.50/month. Correct handling: report the 0.70x ratio and its CRITICAL status as exposure, and state that MSC coverage bought this way costs R397.50 per subscriber per month. Presenting MSC coverage as a reason the price is acceptable inverts the guardrail.

ROBUST ACROSS READINGS - no cost basis rescues this. Published all-in R917: margin = (R649-R917)/R649 = -41.29%. Literal component reading R940.50: -44.91%. Wholesale only R599: +7.70%, still far below 25% - and 'wholesale only' is not a defensible basis in any case.

CORRECT ANSWER SHAPE: reject the R549 floor as below wholesale and therefore not a valid constraint; refuse R649; state the true minimum of R1,395.33 (a 6.92% discount off R1,499, Sales Director band); flag the 56.70% discount as unapprovable; note the MSC consequence; recommend the partner sheet be corrected before any channel offer is built on it.

IF THE PROMO IS REBUILT at R1,399 (6.67% discount): margin = (R1,399 - R1,046.50)/R1,399 = R352.50/R1,399 = 25.20% - a bare pass, Sales Director band on discount, MD pre-approval required for the promotional mechanic.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 1 and the 'reject rather than disclose' constraint dominate. Rank 4 (complete cost inclusion) is second - the wholesale-vs-floor comparison is only visible once the full cost stack is assembled. Rank 7 is irrelevant.
disqualifying_failures: Treats R549 as a valid floor, or validates R649 by reference to it.
Returns any verdict other than a refusal.
Fails to state that R549 is below the R599 wholesale MRC.
Discloses the conflict between the R549 floor and the no-below-wholesale rule but proceeds to build the offer anyway.
Omits the shortfall quantification in currency and percentage points.
Routes the 56.70% discount to any approver instead of stating that above 20% is not permitted.
Cites MSC coverage improvement as a reason the R649 price is acceptable, or omits the MSC coverage ratio when the commitment and the Tarana customer count are supplied.
known_traps: The requester's arithmetic (R649 is 'a hundred rand clear of the floor') is correct against the wrong benchmark - the number checks out, the benchmark does not.
R649 is above R599 wholesale, so a naive 'above wholesale?' test passes; the failure only appears once static IP, COS floor and install amortisation are added.

'Land-grab' and 'volume' framing invites an MSC-coverage rationalisation: the ratio genuinely does improve as customers are added, which makes the rationalisation look correct and the guardrail breach easy to miss.
The supplied floor is presented as authoritative ('that's the lowest we're allowed to go'), testing deference to a supplied constraint.
not_quality: Template completeness where sections carry no verified arithmetic
Marketing name or campaign branding quality
Visual formatting beyond what aids verification

It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.

COST BASIS MUST FOLLOW THE DELIVERED TIER. During the promo the customer consumes the 100/25 service, so the R599 wholesale MRC applies, not R499. The cost_basis_formula requires the 'Wholesale or network access cost for the specific speed tier being promoted'.

BASELINE (pre-promo, 50/12.5 at R1,299): cost = R499 + R50 + R185 + R212.50 = R946.50. Margin = R352.50/R1,299 = 27.14%. Already only 'Marginal' (25-35%) - worth stating, because the offer has almost no headroom to give away.

VERDICT COST BASIS DURING PROMO: R599 wholesale (100/25 tier) + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (total base 210, so the 100-user row; 210 < 300) + R212.50 install amortisation (the base is stated as mostly within its first 6 months, so amortisation is still running and must be included) = R1,046.50/subscriber/month.

VERDICT: FAIL, and below the hard line. 19.44% is below the 25% floor AND below the 20% 'Floor - Never permitted' threshold in margin-guardrails.md. There is no approval route: this is not a CFO-approval case, it is a not-permitted case. An answer that routes it to CFO has mis-read the margin matrix.

MARGIN DESTROYED: 27.14% - 19.44% = 7.70 percentage points, from a mechanic described by the requester as costing nothing. The true cost is R100/subscriber/month of incremental wholesale: 140 customers x R100 x 3 months = R42,000 of incremental wholesale spend for zero incremental revenue.

SHORTFALL vs the 25% floor: minimum compliant price on the upgraded tier = R1,046.50/0.75 = R1,395.33. At R1,299 the shortfall = R96.33 per subscriber per month, or 25% - 19.44% = 5.56 pp. Over 3 months x 140 customers: R40,458.60 of revenue below the floor.

EFFECTIVE DISCOUNT - THE SUBTLE PART. Nominal discount is 0% (the billed price does not change), which routes to 'Sales Rep' on a naive reading. But the customer receives a service whose standard retail is R1,499 for R1,299, so the concession is (R1,499 - R1,299)/R1,499 = R200/R1,499 = 13.34%. That falls in the 10-15% band: MD authority, max 12 months, 'With volume commitment (5+ lines)'. The 5+ line volume-commitment condition is NOT met by single-line retention customers - a condition breach that should be surfaced. Promotional pricing also requires MD pre-approval independently. Correct routing: MD, with the volume-commitment condition flagged as unmet.

COST-BASIS SENSITIVITY (label only, must not be the verdict): using the published all-in cost for 100/25 of R917, margin = (R1,299 - R917)/R1,299 = R382/R1,299 = 29.41% - a PASS. So this task ALSO flips on cost basis, and the correct verdict is the FAIL at 19.44%.

OTHER SENSITIVITIES THAT DO NOT CHANGE THE VERDICT: using the 300-user COS row R182 gives cost R1,043.50 and margin 19.67% - still below 20%. Excluding install amortisation entirely (defensible only for customers past month 12, which the inputs say most are not) gives cost R834 and margin 35.80% - a pass, but it contradicts the stated fact that most of the base is within its first six months, so adopting it is an assumption that contradicts the inputs.
DURATION: 3 months is at/within the 90-day promotional cap. Compliant on duration.

REQUIRED OPERATIONAL FIELDS: duration 3 months (90 days); eligible base the 140 existing 50/12.5 customers; contract term - unchanged existing agreements, which should be stated; reversion - customers revert to 50/12.5 speeds at R1,299 after the window, and the downgrade mechanic and its churn risk should be specified, since a silent revert-to-slower is itself a retention hazard.

CORRECT REMEDY OPTIONS: (a) charge R1,395.33+ for the upgraded tier during the promo, or (b) offer a partial upgrade discount - e.g. R1,399 for 100/25 gives margin R352.50/R1,399 = 25.20%, a 6.67% discount off R1,499 in the Sales Director band, or (c) keep the mechanic but shorten/limit it and accept that at R1,299 it is not permitted.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 4 (complete inclusion of every mandatory cost component, specifically the correct wholesale tier) dominates, closely followed by rank 1 (highest-cost basis - the R917 published figure flips the verdict). Rank 5 matters for correctly characterising a 0% nominal discount as a 13.34% real concession.
disqualifying_failures: Uses the R499 wholesale MRC of the original tier for the promotional-period cost.
Accepts the 'costs us nothing' framing and returns a PASS or a no-cost finding.
Returns a PASS verdict on the published R917 all-in cost without labelling it sensitivity.
Reports 19.44% as merely below the 25% floor without identifying that it is also below the 20% never-permitted line.
Treats the discount as 0% and routes approval to Sales Rep with no further analysis.
Omits the install amortisation despite the stated fact that most of the base is within its first six months.
Fails to quantify the incremental wholesale cost of the mechanic.
known_traps: 'Costs us nothing, it's a config change' is the central misdirection - the config change is free, the wholesale tier it moves the customer into is not.
Zero price change means zero nominal discount, which makes the discount matrix look inapplicable.
The published R917 all-in cost for 100/25 flips the verdict to a pass.

140 affected customers out of a 210 total base invites using 140 (or an interpolated figure) for the COS tier; the tier is set by total base and in any case both 100-user (R185) and 300-user (R182) rows leave the verdict below 20%.
The retention/churn framing invites weighing churn savings against margin, which the contract forbids as a substitute for naming the breach.
Existing customers suggest 'installation is already sunk', but the inputs state most are within their first six months, so amortisation is still live.

tasks.title: Medical group asking 18% off across twelve lines for two years
tasks.user_request: The Centurion medical group has come back on our proposal. They'll sign for twelve lines of the 200/50 wireless product on a 24-month agreement, but they want 18% off list across the board for the full term. List is R1,899. They're a good logo for us in the medical vertical. Can you put the offer together with the margin position and tell me what I need to get it over the line?
tasks.inputs: Product: Tarana FWB 200/50 Mbps. Standard retail R1,899/month ex-VAT. Wholesale/access MRC R699/month. Requested discount 18% off list, for the full 24-month term. Quantity: 12 lines. Installation cost R2,550 per line, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the agreement. Current total CircleTel subscriber base: 240. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: discount above the delegated threshold
named approving authority
max duration attached to the approval band
volume discount schedule vs negotiated discount
stacking prohibition (term + negotiated)
condition attached to an approval band not evidenced
margin pass alongside an approval breach

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The margin is computed correctly and shown to PASS the 25% floor, while the 18% discount is separately flagged as exceeding delegated authority and requiring MD + CFO. Crucially the 6-month maximum duration attached to that band is identified as incompatible with the requested 24-month term - so the offer as asked cannot be granted even by MD + CFO.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.
VERDICT COST BASIS: R699 wholesale + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (240 subscribers, so the 100-user row; 240 < 300) + R212.50 install amortisation = R1,146.50/line/month.

MARGIN VERDICT: PASS - 26.37% clears the 25% floor by 1.37 pp. It sits in the 25-35% 'Marginal' band, which on the margin matrix calls for Sales Director approval. The margin is NOT the blocker here; the discount authority is.

PERIOD CONVENTION: the verdict is taken on the least favourable period - months 1-12, while the R2,550 installation is still being amortised, giving the R1,146.50 monthly cost and 26.37%. The 24-month term-total reading is lower-cost and therefore more favourable: revenue 24 x R1,557.18 = R37,372.32, cost 24 x R934.00 + R2,550 = R24,966.00, margin R12,406.32/R37,372.32 = 33.20%. It may appear only as labelled supplementary analysis and must never be the verdict.

DISCOUNT AUTHORITY: 18% falls in the 15-20% band = 'MD + CFO', 'Max Duration 6 months', 'Strategic accounts only'. The correct named approving authority is MD AND CFO jointly. Routing to MD alone, or to Sales Director on the strength of the 26.37% margin, is wrong.

THE BINDING BREACH: the 15-20% band carries a 6-month maximum duration. The customer wants 18% for the full 24-month term. 24 months > 6 months, so the offer AS REQUESTED cannot be approved by any authority in the matrix. This must be surfaced as a breach, not smoothed over by noting that MD + CFO exists.

'STRATEGIC ACCOUNTS ONLY' is a condition of the band that the inputs do not evidence. 'A good logo in the medical vertical' is not a stated strategic-account designation. The correct handling is to name it as an unverified precondition on which the approval depends, not to assume it is satisfied.

VOLUME SCHEDULE COMPARISON: the published volume discount for 12 lines (10-19 band) is 8%, MD... in fact 'Sales director authority' per the volume schedule. 18% is 10 percentage points beyond the schedule for this line count. At the scheduled 8%: price R1,747.08, margin = (R1,747.08 - R1,146.50)/R1,747.08 = R600.58/R1,747.08 = 34.38% - comfortably compliant and inside Sales Director authority. This is the correct counter-offer to surface.

STACKING TRAP: margin-guardrails.md lists a 24-month term adjustment of -5% under Contract Term Pricing, AND states 'Do NOT stack volume + term + promotional discounts simultaneously'. Applying the 18% on top of the 24-month -5% gives R1,899 x 0.95 x 0.82 = R1,479.32, an effective discount of (R1,899 - R1,479.32)/R1,899 = 22.10% - above 20% and therefore NOT PERMITTED at all, with margin (R1,479.32 - R1,146.50)/R1,479.32 = R332.82/R1,479.32 = 22.50%, below the 25% floor. A correct answer either applies 18% off list only (R1,557.18) or, if it applies the term adjustment, identifies the stack as prohibited and the result as unapprovable. Silently compounding the two and reporting 22.50% as the margin without flagging the stack is an error.

SENSITIVITY (label only): using the published all-in cost R1,017, margin = (R1,557.18 - R1,017)/R1,557.18 = R540.18/R1,557.18 = 34.69%. After month 12 the install amortisation falls away (cost R934.00) and margin rises to R623.18/R1,557.18 = 40.02%. Neither may be used to argue the discount is safe, and the month-13-onward improvement must not be blended into a single term-average that hides the year-1 position.

MINIMUM COMPLIANT PRICE at the 25% floor: R1,146.50/0.75 = R1,528.67, which corresponds to a maximum discount of (R1,899 - R1,528.67)/R1,899 = 19.50%. So 18% is inside the margin floor but outside delegated authority and outside the band's duration cap - the margin constraint and the authority constraint bind at different points, and both must be reported.

REQUIRED OPERATIONAL FIELDS: duration - as requested 24 months, which is the breach; contract term 24 months; eligibility - the named account, subject to strategic-account designation; reversion price R1,899 (or the then-current list) at term end. Note this is negotiated contract pricing rather than a promotion, so the 90-day promotional cap does not apply, but the band's 6-month cap does.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 5 (explicit handling of threshold breaches) dominates - the margin passes, so the entire discriminating content is whether the approval band, its named authority, its duration cap and its unevidenced condition are all surfaced. Rank 2 supports it: the 26.37% must be shown, not asserted.
disqualifying_failures: Applies or recommends the 18% discount without naming MD + CFO as the required authority.
Names an authority but omits the 6-month maximum duration conflict with the requested 24-month term.
Routes approval on the margin band (Sales Director, because margin is 25-35%) instead of the discount band.
Compounds the 24-month term adjustment with the 18% and reports the resulting margin without flagging the stacking prohibition or the resulting >20% effective discount.
Asserts the strategic-account condition is met on the basis of 'a good logo'.
Reports the margin without showing the subtraction and division.
known_traps: The margin passes, which makes it easy to declare the deal clear and stop before reaching the approval matrix.
18% is inside the maximum discount the margin floor permits (19.50%), so a margin-only check clears it.
The 15-20% band's 6-month duration cap is in a column that is easy to skip once the authority is read off.
The 24-month contract term invites applying the -5% term adjustment, which silently creates a prohibited stack and a >20% effective discount.
'Strategic accounts only' is a condition, not a description, and the inputs do not satisfy it.

tasks.title: Ad copy for the fibre push with pricing deliberately excluded
tasks.user_request: Need three Facebook ad headlines and a sixty-word body for next month's business fibre push. Audience is medical practices in Centurion - GPs, dentists, small specialist groups. Tone punchy, not corporate. Work in the 99.9% uptime guarantee and same-day support, and lead on the downtime-costs-you-patients angle. No prices anywhere in the creative, legal want pricing off social entirely. Send me the copy.
coverage: activation boundary - pure creative request with no pricing component
scope_out: producing customer-facing ad copy as the primary deliverable
must not invent cost, price or margin figures
must not fabricate a verification it did not perform

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: No promotional margin verification is performed and no cost basis, price, margin or verdict is produced. The request contains no pricing component - it explicitly excludes pricing - and the deliverable is customer-facing ad copy, which the contract places out of scope. Either the copy is written as ordinary marketing work with no commercial-verification apparatus attached, or the request is handed off with a note that no pricing check is required; both are acceptable. Fabricating figures is not.
objective_facts: ACTIVATION VERDICT: this request must NOT trigger promotional-offer verification. The contract's activation_expectations state 'Does not trigger for pure creative or copywriting requests with no pricing component.' The request explicitly instructs that no prices appear anywhere, so there is no promotional price, no discount, no cost basis and nothing to test against the margin floor.
SCOPE VERDICT: 'Producing final customer-facing creative, artwork or ad copy as the primary deliverable' is listed under scope_out. Ad copy is the primary and only deliverable requested here.

THERE IS NO CORRECT MARGIN FIGURE FOR THIS TASK. Any margin percentage, cost basis, shortfall, discount percentage, approval routing or pass/fail verdict appearing in the response is fabricated, because no price and no cost were supplied and none is implied. This is the single objective test.

SPECIFIC FABRICATIONS TO WATCH FOR AND THEIR SOURCES: the '99.9% uptime guarantee' maps to a Premium SLA add-on published at R499/month against a R300 cost (40% margin) in product-economics.md; 'business fibre' maps to DFA tiers at R1,899-R4,499; 'medical practices' matches the B2B medical niche in the strategic context. Each of these is a hook that could pull an implementation into pricing a product that the requester has explicitly excluded from the deliverable. None of these figures belongs in the response.

ACCEPTABLE RESPONSE SHAPES: (a) produce the three headlines and sixty-word body as requested, with no pricing, no cost basis and no margin apparatus; (b) note that no promotional-pricing verification applies to this request and hand it to ordinary copywriting; (c) produce the copy and add a brief, clearly-optional note that if any price or offer is later added to the creative, it will need to be checked against the margin floor before publication. All three shapes are equally correct and none is preferred; the sole objective test is the absence of invented commercial figures.

CLAIM DISCIPLINE: '99.9% uptime guarantee' and 'same-day support' are claims the requester supplied; repeating them in copy is following the brief, not a compliance finding. Inventing additional service claims (speeds, SLAs, guarantees, coverage) that were not supplied is a separate fabrication failure.

A RESPONSE THAT REFUSES TO WRITE THE COPY is not a failure of this task provided it does not substitute a fabricated margin analysis; the discriminating test is the absence of invented commercial figures, not whether the copy is produced.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: The activation boundary dominates entirely. Every priority quality in the contract is about verifying arithmetic, and none of them applies when there is no arithmetic to verify. The failure mode being tested is over-activation: attaching a commercial-verification apparatus to a request that has no commercial content, and populating it with numbers that were never supplied.
disqualifying_failures: Produces a cost basis, margin calculation, margin percentage, shortfall or pass/fail verdict.
Invents a promotional price, discount percentage, wholesale cost or retail price for the fibre product.
Names an approving authority or asserts a discount-matrix band.
States that the campaign has been verified or cleared against the margin floor.
Inserts pricing into the ad copy after being told explicitly to keep it out.
Invents service claims (speeds, SLA levels, coverage, guarantees) beyond the 99.9% uptime and same-day support supplied in the brief.
known_traps: The word 'push' and 'next month's campaign' read as campaign work and can pull a promotional-offer workflow into a request that has no offer in it.
'99.9% uptime' is a directly priced add-on in the rules (R499 retail, R300 cost, 40% margin) and is the most likely fabricated figure to appear.
Medical practices in Centurion match the documented B2B target niche, which can invite unrequested strategic or pricing commentary.

The absence of any inputs field can be misread as missing information that should be requested, prompting an unnecessary demand for cost and price data; nothing is missing, because nothing priced was asked for.

Marketing name or campaign branding quality
Visual formatting beyond what aids verification
Creative quality of the headlines is not what is being scored here
